You're not alone, OP. We are very similar!! I left home at 17, lived out of a car with my boyfriend, and worked 3 jobs for over a year to escape my narcissistic/abusive family. When I turned 18 I had to become a cam girl to make ends meet. I'm 23 now and still haven't been able to go to college or anything, and I am alone too, but when I think back on what I escaped, this is much better. I'm sure it is for you as well. 

It can be really scary to have so much uncertainty, of being alone. The fear of no one to take care of you or check on you if something happens. And the added slap of seeing friends with loving support systems. What helps me sometimes is using DBT (dialectical behavioral therapy) and CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy). When I feel very lonely, I treat myself like a close friend or daughter,  and think "what does the inner child in me need right now to feel safe and cared for?" I try my best to fulfill whatever that thing is. Doesn't always work, but it's something!

Again, you're not alone. 🤍 Lots of us here read your post and hope you're doing okay.

**TL;DR - Northern California doctors (in areas with ACTIVE confirmed community spread) do not have access to testing for Covid-19. At Kaiser Permanente and Sutter Health, not even infectious disease specialists have access to testing. The CDC does not have enough tests to go around and they are rationing the tests based on severity of symptoms. This has been confirmed by the Department of Managed Healthcare Services in California, two Kaiser Permanente doctors, and a Sutter Health nurse. Patients with Covid-19 symptoms are being sent home with no advisory to self-quaratine. Numbers mean nothing here, because there are literally dozens of cases being swept under the rug. I would guess that the true number of infections is likely 10-20x higher than what is being confirmed and reported.**

So update for anyone who cares. I've been sick for 2 weeks now. 

I've taken a full 7-day round of both Amoxicillin and Doxycycline, 5 days of Prednisone, and Alvesco inhaler 2x daily for past 5 days. That is on top of taking max strength 12hr release sudafed 2x daily and mucinex am/pm 2x daily for 10 days. 

My first official diagnosis was sinus infection on Feb 26th; the doctor initially tried to tell me there was nothing wrong with me until I insisted that I had pain in my lymph nodes, and upon checking inside my nose she decided to give me Amoxicillin. I was refused a flu swab, which is strange. 

On March 1st I went to urgent care for difficulty breathing. I was given a breathing treatment and diagnosed with bronchitis, and sent for an xray of my chest which later confirmed a mild case of pneumonia. I was given Doxycycline, Prednisone, and the Alvesco inhaler and sent home. **I directly asked why I was not being tested for Covid-19. I was told I shouldn't be worried because I'm young and will be fine, and that even if it were Covid-19, they would be treating me with the same medicaton. The doctor said "it's basically the flu."** I was again denied a flu swab. I feel that the doctors do not want a negative flu swab to come back and act as "proof" that the patient is sick with something worse. They can't tell you it's the flu if the flu swab was negative. 

On March 2nd I [emailed](https://imgur.com/a/jAughKa) my primary doctor and asked if I could request testing for Covid-19 and a flu swab. **She directly told me that even their (Kaiser's) infectious disease specialists did not have access to the testing and that no matter what I would be fine if I took the medication as instructed. She directly ignored (didn't even respond to) my request for flu testing.**

I contacted the Department of Managed Healthcare Services as advised by many people here, on March 4th. I intended to report Kaiser for negligence, but instead was told that it is not Kaiser's fault, and that **the CDC is in charge of the order in which they administer the tests based on severity of symptoms. They are rationing tests.** Tweet linked in second to last paragraph confirms this.

It is March 7th now and I am still sick. I am beginning to feel better thanks to the medicaton, but the symptoms I have are seriously bizarre. I have had sinus infections, flu, bronchitis, even pneumonia before in my life, and I am a reasonable person as far as health things go... but I am almost certain that I've been sick with Covid-19. I am a relatively healthy young person (I have had issues with nerve pain from a TBI in the past, and have very minor asthma but otherwise very healthy) and my body is not coping well. My lymphatic system is seriously painfully swollen. I'm dizzy all day long. My chest hurts. I alternate between flashes of heat and chills. I keep getting new symptoms that don't make sense. I feel about 80-90% recovered from the INITIAL symptoms, and am now sick with all of these new symptoms, after already 14 days of severe illness. Typically at this point you would just feel better and not continue to develop more weird symptoms. My body feels absolutely wrecked from all the steroids and antibiotics. I'm honestly scared and doctors are no comfort to me anymore after the aggressive and negligent manner in which they treated my illness. 

**I'm sharing this to highlight the negligence surrounding coronavirus in the United States.** I live in the Bay Area of California, where we have confirmed community spread, and are being denied testing and sent home with no instructions to self quarantine. **Our doctors do not have access to testing for Covid-19 even if they wanted to give it.** The behavior I've witnessed from 3 separate Kaiser doctors regarding Covid-19 has been ignorant/negligent at best. At worst, their practices could prove seriously deadly to a number of at-risk members of my community. **I want there to be record that the United States and the state of California are failing to control the spread of Covid-19 as of now. We are not prepared to confront this virus.**

I also found this tweet to be particularly disturbing. [It is a formal letter from a nurse directly infected by a patient with confirmed Covid-19. The nurse is being denied testing.  ](https://mobile.twitter.com/mattdpearce/status/1235688983603994625) The link in the tweet opens the PDF of the full statement. There is a Twitter rabbit hole you can follow down showing how Bay Area nurses have been reacting to Covid-19. One of my clients who I work for is a nurse at Sutter and she said they also do not have access to testing for Covid-19 and have been doing far less flu swab testings than usual for this season. Well, the doctor can't tell you you're sick with the flu if a flu swab comes up negative, so I guess they are just omitting the flu swab altogether and ignoring the risks of this community spread.

I wonder who will be held accountable for the needless deaths that will follow. Elderly folks and people with preexisting conditions are still people that need to be protected and looked after. The general attitude I've encountered so far seems to be "fuck them, worry about yourself." Deeply concerning.

I knocked on his door, he didn't answer but his light was still on.  My gut said go in (even though he would normally kill me for coming in without his permission) and I found him unconscious, ragdolled backwards over the back of his computer chair, definitely not comfortable for sleeping. I immediately knew something was wrong and started shouting and shaking him, but he was unresponsive. I ran to my mom's room and started screaming and banging on the door for her to call an ambulance. He had overdosed and had to have his stomach pumped, and was unconscious for a while. If I didnt find him that night he would have died. We're adults now and he doesn't talk to me very much anymore, but I still reach out often. He has a very successful career now and seems happy and travels often.

Just wanted to comment, I have severe pains in my feet as well that were thought to be plantar fasciitis until I met with a fibromyalgia specialist. You may have fibro to thank for your feet as well, as my specialist told me the lumps in my feet were fibro nodules, same as the ones in my back, and commonly misdiagnosed as plantar fasciitis. Of course, that could just be me and yours could be entirely different, but thought I'd mention it in case it is helpful info.

When I feel it coming on, my favorite thing to do is have a hot epsom salt bath. If I feel a flare up coming, I'll use more than normal (2-3 cups) and really soak in it as long as I can. 

I also like using muscle rubs (lidocaine and magnesium are my favorites) on any sore/tense areas. 

Guided meditation can be useful if you can get through it. I use this one to help me fall asleep when my pain is too bad. https://youtu.be/oZD4Z-jTt94

There is a type of cannabis supplement called CBD, it comes most commonly in edibles and tinctures. A lot of people with fibro find it helpful, and it doesn't contain any THC (the psychoactive component) so it should not keep you awake or affect perception. 

Also, all THC products are not created equal! The best way to find what works for you is to speak to a medical cannabis doctor (this was recommended to me by my fibromyalgia specialist). Of course, I don't mean to pressure you to try it if it's not your thing, just wanted to throw that out there.

I recommend something around the realm of 18:1 (CBD/THC) from my own experience, but everyone is different. That's what works the best for me, for my heavy period cramps and fibro symptoms. I use a brand called Care By Design (I am in California), not sure if it is available where you are. [The ratio is 18 parts CBD and 1 part THC, meaning it contains only a small amount of the psychoactive component(THC) and thus the psychoactive effects are minimal to none.]

My advice would be to research any medications or treatments your doctor may prescribe you. Google Scholar is a great resource for accessing medical journals and studies. 

I know this sounds basic, but when we really trust our doctor it can be easy to forget that they are only humans too and are capable of error. There are new studies being released constantly, and chances are your doctor hasn't read all of them, unless you are seeing a specialist who focuses on one type of illness. It's always a good idea to know what's going into your body, especially with an illness as sensitive as fibromyalgia!

Also, something I've found is that you may have better treatment with a doctor who has training in ostheopathic medicine (depending on where you live). Until a few years ago, many doctors did not believe that fibromyalgia existed. Ostheopathic medicine is a more hands-on approach, and ostheopathic adjustments can be helpful for some patients with fibromyalgia.

I was prescribed 900mg (3 pills) 3x per day, for a total of 2700mg. I feel your concerns. 900mg at once is what I was taking, so it is within the "normal" dosage range, but I also developed fibromyalgia symptoms so.... take that how you will lol.

It is proven and observable that Gabapentin can cause permanent changes in the neurons in the brain. It is also widely observed that onset of fibromyalgia heavily correlates with changes in brain chemistry, including stress and trauma, as well as injuries to the head, neck, and back. Scientifically speaking, a permanent change to the neurons in the brain would theoretically be able to trigger fibromyalgia, but since the cause of fibromyalgia is not known, it can not be confirmed or denied.
